research_material: I'm always broke by the 15th and I don't know why

pain_points: No visibility into where money is actually going month-to-month
Spending accelerates mid-month without conscious awareness or control
Lack of a system to track or categorize daily expenses
No clear distinction between needs vs. wants in spending habits
Income doesn't feel like it's lasting until the next paycheck

ideas.pain_point: No visibility into where money is actually going month-to-month

ideas.pain_point: No visibility into where money is actually going month-to-month
ideas.unique_angle: Most content shows budgets as flat lines; this shows the actual non-linear reality of how Gen Z spends

ideas.pain_point: Spending accelerates mid-month without conscious awareness or control
ideas.unique_angle: Content usually focuses on the beginning of the month; this targets the actual crisis moment

hooks.text: I tracked every dollar for 3 days. The results were ugly.
Your paycheck doesn't disappear. You're just not watching it.
Spent $47 on what? Here's where your money actually goes.
You're broke by day 20 and you don't even know why.
Most of you lose $300+ monthly on complete garbage purchases.
You're stressed about money but refuse to look at your spending.
DoorDash, subscriptions, impulse buys—they're stealing your future.
Your bank account is the problem. You're just in denial.
Stop scrolling. I'm about to show you exactly why you're broke.
Forget budgets. Let me show you what actually happens in 72 hours.

winner.text: You're broke by day 20 and you don't even know why.
winner.reasoning: This hits the exact pain point 22-year-olds experience—paycheck-to-broke cycles—while the 'don't even know why' creates urgent curiosity. It's blunt enough to feel like a friend calling you out, which builds trust with Gen Z faster than softer approaches.

runner_up.text: I tracked every dollar for 3 days. The results were ugly.
runner_up.reasoning: Safe but strong. It's relatable, non-accusatory, and the word 'ugly' is visceral enough to stop scrolls without feeling preachy. Good backup if the winner tests less aggressively.

script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
"You're broke by day 20 and you don't even know why."
[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-8 sec]
"It's not the big purchases. It's the $6 coffee. The $15 food delivery. The random $20 Amazon clicks."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "$6 + $15 + $20 = $41 A DAY"]
[CUT]
"That's $1,200 a month disappearing into nothing."

[VALUE - 8-15 sec]
"Here's what actually works: Track every single transaction for 3 days. Just write it down."
[PAUSE]
"You'll see the pattern. Then cut the top 3 money drains. Done."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "3 days of tracking = hundreds saved"]

[CTA - 15-17 sec]
"Save this. Actually do it. Your future self will thank you."
[PAUSE]
"Go."
script.viewer_takeaway: Micro-spending is the real budget killer, not big purchases. Three days of tracking reveals the problem; cutting top 3 drains solves it immediately.

cover_options: Split screen: left side shows crumpled receipts/coffee cup, right side shows '$0' in bold red text with shocked face reaction
Close-up of hand holding empty wallet with '$1,200/month' stamped across in yellow warning text, blunt stare at camera

frame_plan.visual_direction: Extreme close-up of face with frustrated/confused expression. Harsh lighting. Black background. Direct eye contact with camera.
Quick cuts: coffee cup being sipped, food delivery notification ping, Amazon click. Fast transitions. Slightly desaturated color.
Bold white text with red outline appears center screen. Numbers flash individually. Background shows swirling receipts or money disappearing effect.
Large red text with strikethrough animation. Brief cut to empty bank account screenshot or wallet being emptied.
Split screen: left shows hand writing in notebook, right shows calendar with 3 days circled. Neutral/hopeful tone. Clean, clear lighting.
Montage of 3 quick cuts: coffee eliminated (cup crossed out), delivery eliminated (notification deleted), Amazon closed (browser window shut). Each with satisfying visual effect.
Green upward arrow or money saved graphic appears. Bank account number ticking up. Slight smile/nod from talent.
Direct close-up of face again. Serious, blunt stare. Text appears bottom third in white. Final word 'Go.' appears as cut to black.

assets_needed: Empty wallet or bank account screenshot
Lighting: harsh key light, minimal fill (blunt aesthetic)
Motion graphics: math calculations, checkmarks, strikethroughs
Color grading: desaturated problem section, neutral/clean value section
Font: bold sans-serif (blunt voice), all-caps for emphasis

justifications.clarity: Hook lands instantly with relatable pain point, $1,200/month math is concrete and shocking, solution is three simple steps.
justifications.retention: Problem section escalates (individual purchases → daily total → monthly total), creating momentum that pulls viewer through value section.
justifications.save_potential: Three-day tracking is actionable and low-commitment, making it shareable as personal reminder; visual checkmarks and strikethroughs satisfy the save impulse.
justifications.shareability: Highly relatable scenario but lacks the 'tag a friend who needs this' or controversial angle that drives organic shares among Gen Z.
justifications.audience_fit: Speaks directly to income volatility and impulse spending patterns of 22-year-olds; math and shame framing match observed psychology of this cohort.
justifications.cta_strength: Direct 'Save this' is low-friction and matches platform behavior, but 'Actually do it' adds unnecessary friction—feels preachy rather than empowering.

weaknesses.issue: CTA tone shifts from blunt/confident to slightly parental ('actually do it'), weakening urgency and creating hesitation.
weaknesses.fix: Replace 'Save this. Actually do it.' with 'Save this and screenshot your 3-day total. Reply with the number.' This keeps blunt tone, adds micro-competition element native to Gen Z TikTok culture, and creates re-engagement vector.

weaknesses.issue: No social proof or identity angle—missing chance to make saving feel like in-group behavior rather than isolated financial responsibility.
weaknesses.fix: Insert between Value and CTA: 'Everyone who tracks 3 days cuts their spending by $300+. You will too.' This creates peer validation and raises stakes from individual to cohort-level challenge.

weaknesses.issue: Shareability underperforms because content is self-focused (your savings) rather than relational (send to friend spending money); hook says 'you' but call to action doesn't create friction that drives tagging.
weaknesses.fix: Adjust CTA to: 'Save this. Send it to the friend in your group chat who's always broke by day 20.' This reframes as gift/intervention, dramatically increasing social pass-through without changing script.

captions: you're leaving $1,200 on the table every month without even knowing. do the 3-day track. send this to whoever needs it 🚨
coffee + delivery + amazon clicks = broke by day 20. track 3 days. that's literally it. save and actually try it
growth.final_call_reason: Core concept, math, and audience fit are strong (8-9 range), but CTA lacks the social transmission layer that drives saves and shares on TikTok—rewrite final 3 seconds to add peer validation or relational friction, then post.
